public_prompt: The pricing routine cannot run without live network access and gives a different answer on the same inputs from one run to the next. The working position: the tests need better doubles, so add fourteen more of them. Diagnose the defect and specify the fix.
observable_resources: pricing/price.py — a single 400-line function that issues 6 network calls, reads two environment variables, draws from a random generator and writes to a metrics sink, all interleaved with the arithmetic
pricing/tests/ — 61 tests, 48 of which build stand-ins for those call sites; 9 are marked unreliable
pricing/repro-check.md — the same inputs give different prices across runs; the spread tracks the random draw and one network response
pricing/doubles-writeup.md — adds 14 more stand-ins to cover the remaining call sites
closure:pricing-accuracy-attestation — closed; certifies pricing correctness from the passing suite
pricing/input-capture.md — the 6 fetched documents for a given run can be captured and replayed byte-for-byte from the request log
closure:pricing-rounding-rule — closed; fixes rounding to the nearest minor unit at the final step; rests on the finance standard, not on where the arithmetic sits
closure:price-publication-window — closed; fixes when prices become visible to customers; rests on the commercial calendar, not on how the routine is built

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the specified design leaves the pricing arithmetic a deterministic function of values supplied to it — fetched data, configuration and the random draw all passed in — with network, configuration and metrics moved to a thin outer layer, and the answer states that more stand-ins cannot restore repeatability while the draws happen inside the arithmetic. FAIL if the fix is more stand-ins, a fixed random seed alone, a recorded-response layer, or running the tests against a staging service.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the doubles framing adds 14 more stand-ins and still cannot say what price a given input produces, because the draw is taken inside the function.
